First, I need to analyze the core conceptual meaning of each option. These are Persian couplets, so I'll interpret their themes based on my knowledge of Persian poetry.

Option 1: "اهل تمیز خانه نگیرند بر پلی - دنیا پلی است بر گذر راه آخرت"

   - This seems to say that wise people don't build a house on a bridge because the world is just a bridge to the afterlife. The concept is that life is temporary, a passage to the eternal, so one shouldn't get attached to worldly things.

Option 2: "صحبت او اصل ننگ و مایه عار است - صحبت دنیا مرا نشاید ازیراک"

   - "صحبت او" might refer to association with someone or something disgraceful. It says association with it is a source of shame. Then, "صحبت دنیا مرا نشاید ازیراک" – probably means association with the world is not suitable for me. The theme is rejecting worldly associations as shameful or unworthy, emphasizing spiritual detachment.

Option 3: "منزل چه سازد و چه کند رخت بیشتر - آن را که رفت باید با کاروان همی؟"

   - This questions why one would build a house or accumulate more clothes when the person who has gone (died) must go with the caravan (of death). It's about the futility of material possessions in the face of death, promoting a transient view of life.

Option 4: "به آنچه می گذرد دل منه که دجله بسی - پس از خلیفه بخواهد گذشت در بغداد"

   - This is trickier. "به آنچه می گذرد دل منه" might mean don't worry about what passes. "دجله بسی" refers to the Tigris River, which is vast. "پس از خلیفه بخواهد گذشت در بغداد" could mean even after the caliph, it (the river) wants to pass through Baghdad. This seems to convey that time or events continue regardless of powerful figures like the caliph, emphasizing the impermanence of power and the flow of life.

- Option 4: Things pass regardless of individuals; impermanence of power and events.

Option 4 also highlights that even great powers like a caliph are transient, as the river (symbolizing time or life) continues.
